title: Deconfounding Legal Judgment Prediction for European Court of Human Rights Cases Towards Better Alignment with Experts

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating and mitigating the model's reliance on the identity of the respondent state (country) using a multi-class discriminator and adversarial training with a Gradient Reversal Layer (GRL), then assessing the alignment of model focus with legal expert rationales using Integrated Gradients.

Identifying shallow, legally irrelevant predictive artifacts (such as document length, paragraph numbers, and distractor vocabulary like 'represented') using simple decision tree models, mitigating their effects through adversarial discriminators, and evaluating the resulting feature attribution using Integrated Gradients against expert annotations.
